topics.title: Introduction: the two writers and their works

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the two writers, their communities and the focus of the unit.
Explain the meaning and the pun in the title 'Karukku'.

topics.title: Zitkala-Sa: the first day at school
topics.ncert_sections: I. The Cutting of My Long Hair (the dining room)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the strange school surroundings and dress affected Zitkala-Sa.
Explain the bell-controlled breakfast and why she calls it 'eating by formula'.

topics.title: Zitkala-Sa: the cutting of her long hair
topics.ncert_sections: I. The Cutting of My Long Hair (the haircut)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what long and shingled hair meant among Zitkala-Sa's people.
Analyse Zitkala-Sa's resistance and her sense of humiliation when her hair is cut.

topics.title: Bama: the walk home and the elder with the vadais
topics.ncert_sections: II. We Too are Human Beings (the bazaar and the threshing floor)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the sights that delayed Bama and explain why she describes them so fully.
Interpret the scene of the elder carrying the packet to the landlord.

topics.title: Bama: Annan's explanation and advice
topics.ncert_sections: II. We Too are Human Beings (Annan's words)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Annan reveals the practice of untouchability to Bama.
Evaluate Annan's advice that study can help throw away indignities.
Identify the common theme of the two accounts from distant cultures.
Compare the kinds of discrimination the two girls face and their responses.
